## Prototype scope

The prototype is an expanded Diplomacy set in one era, not a grand-strategy game. Its only job is to test the core hypothesis cheaply; every system that does not feed trust, mediation or verification is cut. The table records that first scope. The build order goes further, item by item, and where an item takes something from the right-hand column, the row says so.

| Area | In the prototype | Deliberately out (for now) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Players | Seven Great Kings, each a seat | Vassals as seats, more than seven powers (city-states become powers with build order item 11+) |
| Era | Late Bronze Age only | Eras, tech tree, trust progression |
| Economy | Gold from provinces, unit upkeep, transfers | Population, trade goods, markets for goods |
| Military | Armies and fleets, Diplomacy-style resolution, plus sieges, walls and minimal terrain (pillar 8) | Unit types, logistics of supply (distance-based marching is decided: build order item 13) |
| Communication | Envoys with delay, agency and bribery | Separate scribes, translators, couriers |
| Characters | Pool of 18 envoys and spies with hidden facts; planned: one pool of generalist characters who can also serve as generals and governors | Dynasties, heirs |
| Evidence | Sealed tablets, authentication, basic forgery | Notaries, witnesses as systems (archives at the capital come with build order item 3) |
| World | Seeded catastrophes, hidden from outsiders | Religion, culture, internal politics |
| Goal | Relative growth score, random end | Hidden objectives, sandbox mode |
| Presentation | Text reports, an atmospheric spectator map (planned next: see Spectator mode), spectator mode for AI-only games | Commissioned art, sound |

Vassal city-states exist only as neutral provinces that can be taken or bought. A power can buy a neutral city that borders its land or troops, or lies one sea zone from its coast, and a city that has accepted a patron's gold defends its walls. Both rules are in testing. This holds until build order item 11+, which makes city-states powers of their own and removes buying ("One scoreboard for every power" under Victory). From the economy's first phase (item 9+a) until then, a neutral city has a market and a people's purse but no king: its production stays with its people, nobody taxes it or sets tolls there, and any power's caravans may trade at its market.
